chapter_theme: Pambatti's boast of the Siddhars' powers, then his first sermon on detachment. The boasts (2005 to 2013) are hyperbole in the first person plural: making Adishesha dance, turning a pillar to a straw, drinking the seven seas, bending the sky as a bow, turning three worlds to gold, creating like Brahma and living as the Lord's equal, with the sixty-four arts and the one beyond them. A short dialogue section (2014 to 2018), without the refrain, sets the eight nagas in a chakra of eight directions with letters, mantra and ash. The sermon (2019 to 2029) turns to the hearer: land, armies, jewels, mansions, gold, feasts, finery, kin and the beauty of women all stay behind when Yama comes, and only the one who has set his heart on the Lord does not perish.
structure_note: Three printed sections: சித்தர் வல்லபங் கூறல் continued (2005 to 2013), சித்தர் சம்வாதம் (2014 to 2018, each stanza ending சித்தனாரே, a Siddhar addressing Siddhars), பொருளாசை விலக்கல் (2019 to 2028) and the first stanza of பெண்ணாசை விலக்கல் (2029, continued in chapter 104). The boasts in 2007, 2009, 2012 are addressed to a king (மகாராஜன், தார்வேந்தன், மன்னன்), which suggests performance before a court; the sermon stanzas each name one class of possession and end with the same verdict.

2005.reading: Even if it be Adishesha himself, we will make him dance with our hand within our command, and make him stand there joined to right, without falling from the state in which he stands; dance.
2005.nuance: ஆக்கினை (ஆஞ்ஞை), command, is the key word: the Siddhar claims authority over the cosmic serpent that bears the earth. On the coded reading Adishesha is the kundalini held steady (நின்ற நிலை தவறாமல்) once raised.

2006.reading: We will make a pillar appear as a small straw and a straw appear as a great pillar, we will make a man a woman and a woman a man; stand before them with a roar and dance.
2006.nuance: தோன்றிடச் செய்வோம், make it appear, admits that these are shows of appearance; the stanza's own verb puts the power on the side of illusion rather than substance. Pillar and straw correspond to the siddhis of greatness and minuteness.

2007.reading: We will pick up the eight mountains and throw them like balls, drink the seven seas and belch, and count the uncountable sand; stand before the great king and dance.
2007.nuance: The eight mountains are the guardians of the eight directions and the seven seas the puranic oceans; the boast is of cosmic scale. மகாராஜன் முன்பு places the performance before a king.

2008.reading: We will hide the whole earth with our hand, bend the sky itself as a bow, and show the void to our followers by telling of it; stand before the prince and dance.
2008.nuance: சூனியம் சொல்லிக் காட்டுவோம் can mean teaching the followers the void of 1987 by speech, or showing them a conjuring (சூனியம் as sorcery in common Tamil); in a stanza of stage-feats both readings stand, and the ambiguity may be the poet's.

2009.reading: We will plunge into blazing fire and come out, hold our breath though we sit in the three waters, and strike down the strong tiger that leaps at us; stand before the garlanded king and dance.
2009.nuance: மூச்சு அடக்குவோம், holding the breath under water, is the one feat in the list that is also a practice: breath control is the Siddhars' method, and here it is displayed as a power.

2010.reading: We will turn the three worlds that cannot be described into red gold, make the hot sun's rays cool, and make this great world not exist; see our power and dance.
2010.nuance: Turning the worlds to gold extends the alchemist's transmutation to the cosmos; making the world not exist is read traditionally as the jnani's dissolving of the world in the void, as well as a feat of illusion.

2011.reading: We will make creations other than those Brahma made, we will make Brahma himself stand beneath us, and we will live equal with the Lord; this is what we do, dance.
2011.nuance: நாதனுடன் சமமாக வாழ்வோம், living as the Lord's equal, is the peak of the boasts, and it sits oddly with the song's worship of the Lord's feet (1980 to 1988); the Siddhar claim of becoming Siva and the charmer's bravado are hard to separate here.

2012.reading: We have known all the sixty-four arts, and we have known the one art above them; we have a mind without the least attachment to anything else; king, we are the teacher, dance.
2012.nuance: அதற்கு மேல் ஒரு கலை, the one art above the sixty-four, is not named; tradition takes it as the knowledge of the self or of the breath. மன்னனே யாசான் is read as the Siddhar telling the king that he, the Siddhar, is the master (ஆசான்), the inversion that closes the court boasts.

2013.reading: We will order the small tiger, the elephant, the yali and the lion to do menial service for our small feet, and we will make the great mighty God play along with us; dance.
2013.nuance: The boast ends not with mastery of God but with making him a playmate (எங்களுடனே விளையாடச் செய்குவோம்), answering 1988 where the Lord's creation was his own play.

2014.reading: Set Vasuki on one side, king, and the great Padman on the other, join the shining Takshan in his direction, and take the red Padman, Siddhars.
2014.nuance: The dialogue stanzas lay out the eight nagas in the directions as a snake-charmer's or sorcerer's diagram. Padman is named twice (பதுமன் and செய்ய பதுமன்), and one of them should be Mahapadman to complete the eight; the stanza does not say what the arrangement is for.

2015.reading: Set Anantan on one side, join Gulikan beside him near the egg, and show the heavy Karkotakan so that he sees, and the fierce Sankhapalan, Siddhars.
2015.nuance: With 2014 this completes the eight nagas. அண்டச் சேர்த்து, joined near, may hide அண்டம், the egg or cosmos, in which case the diagram is the cosmos itself; the syntax of காணக் காட்டும் (show so as to see) is loose.

2016.reading: Scoring the eight directions as chakras, setting the letters in the places of the angles, recite the mantra with resolve and stand; do not let your mind waver, Siddhars.
2016.nuance: This is the yantra procedure of the Tirumanthiram's chakra tantra in miniature: draw, place letters at the corners, recite. சித்தம் தடுமாறாதீர், do not waver, is the only instruction about the practitioner's inner state in the whole section.

2017.reading: We have set up chakras in the eight directions, we have set up chakras in each of them, and we have placed them where the eight nagas are; tell us what to do now, Siddhars.
2017.nuance: The second speaker reports the work done and asks for the next step, so the section is a real dialogue between a teacher and practitioners. The doubled line (chakras in each) suggests chakras within chakras, or is a copyist's repetition.

2018.reading: Plant Adishesha himself in the middle, scatter mantra-charged ash to the four directions, and take the hooded ones in your hands and dance so that they spit out their fierce poison, Siddhars.
2018.nuance: The rite closes with the serpent at the centre, consecrated ash (மந்திரித்த நீறு) and the handling of cobras until they discharge venom, which is 2004's boast performed. On the traditional reading the centre is the suzhumunai and the poison the mind's passions; the stanza's own words are a charmer's.

2019.reading: Will country and town, house and cattle and all your fine goods seek you out and come when the arbiter arrives? Once the cage is gone, what profit do you get from them? Fix your aim on the Dancer's feet and dance.
2019.nuance: நடுவன், the impartial one, is Yama, and கூடு (the cage) is the body. The sermon's first stanza sets its pattern: a list of possessions, the question whether they come along at death, and the turn to the feet of the Dancer (கூத்தன்).

2020.reading: Elephants, armies, chariots and horses, every one of them: understand that they will be no help when Yama comes; dance so that sense comes to the dogs who have not the least knowledge.
2020.nuance: The hearers are நாய்கள், dogs without knowledge; the abuse is part of the Siddhars' sermon style, and the snake's dance is meant to teach them.

2021.reading: Ruby, great gem crowns and armlets, pendants hanging on the chest and other jewels, pure gold, pearl strings, gold anklets and bracelets: stand knowing them as goods that perish, and dance.
2021.nuance: A catalogue stanza; the verdict is only the last line, அழிவான பொருள். The jewels are a king's, continuing the court setting of 2007 to 2012.

2022.reading: Upper storeys, halls and mansions, painted pavilions, palaces girt with walls and all such things will not come along; those who know this truth do not take pride in them but turn from them in distaste; dance.
2022.nuance: வெறுப்பார், they will feel distaste, is stronger than detachment: the knower of the கொள்கை (the principle that nothing accompanies) comes to dislike what others prize.

2023.reading: Those who have kept heaps of red gold like mountains, will they sweep them up and go when Death comes? Those who without wavering set their heart on the Father will not perish; be sure of it and dance.
2023.nuance: The stanza pairs its two halves: the hoarders cannot carry gold away, the devotees do not perish (அழியார்). The claim is not that devotees avoid death but that something in them does not end.

2024.reading: Will cotton beds, flower beds and mats be of any use in that bare burning ground? Know clearly that the scent of turmeric will go and the stench of burning will come, and dance.
2024.nuance: The contrast is of smells: மஞ்சள் மணம், the turmeric of the bath and the bed, against சுடு நாறும் மணம், the smell of the pyre. The body is seen from its end.

2025.reading: The mouth that first ate the three fruits, sugar, sweetmeats and ripe-tasting dainties: once the great life has gone it swallows earth; we have seen this to be true, so dance.
2025.nuance: மண்ணை விழுங்க, swallowing earth, is the buried or burnt mouth; the stanza reverses the eating. மெய்யாகக் கண்டோம், we saw it truly, is the Siddhar's appeal to his own observation rather than scripture.

2026.reading: Coloured silks and perfumes and the well-made adornment, the fine umbrella, the round fan and the other insignia will certainly not be able to come along at the time of going to Yama's city; dance.
2026.nuance: கவிகை (umbrella), ஆலவட்டம் (circular fan) and சின்னம் (insignia) are royal emblems; the sermon is still addressed to the king of the boasts.

2027.reading: Children, wife, kin, sons-in-law and the rest do not die together with one when one dies; so leap and leap and praise the Maker who gave this whole fitting world, and dance.
2027.nuance: The kin fail not by faithlessness but by the plain fact that they do not die with you (கூட மாள்வதில்லை). The only relation that holds is to the one who gave the world.

2028.reading: Like a deer that takes a mirage for water and goes after it, fools see the life of this earth and rejoice; those who have seen the higher state do not talk empty bluster, but seek the feet of the True One; dance.
2028.nuance: The mirage-deer (கானல்மான்) closes the section on possessions by naming the error: not that wealth is bad but that it is not what it seems. மேனிலை கண்டார், those who have seen the higher state, are set against the வீம்பு (vaunting) of the world, which sits uneasily with the Siddhar's own boasts in 2005 to 2013.

2029.reading: Men who desire women's beauty, which is like turmeric that has seen the sun, and fall upon it and join it, will run off when the body goes, like the parrot that guarded the silk-cotton tree and flew away on seeing its pod; dance.
2029.nuance: Two similes: turmeric paste that fades in sunlight for beauty, and the proverb of the parrot that waited on the silk-cotton fruit, found it empty cotton and fled, for the lover's disappointment. The section on desire for women opens with the lover's own flight, not yet with the body's filth.

links.note: Tirumular's eight siddhis begin with being an atom within the atom and greatness; Pambatti's pillar made a straw and straw made a pillar are the same pair of powers as a stage show. Tirumular presents them as attainments of yoga; Pambatti's own verb, make it appear, admits they are appearances.

Tirumular says he has learned the way of sending moon, fire and sun up the path, the inner alchemy of the breath; Pambatti boasts of turning the three worlds to red gold and cooling the sun. Both move the alchemist's vocabulary from metal to cosmos, Tirumular inward and Pambatti outward.

Tirumular says letters, songs and the sixty-four arts do not remove birth; Pambatti, having known the sixty-four, says he knows the one art above them and has a mind without attachment. Both set the whole curriculum below one knowledge, which Tirumular names as the way of the breath and Pambatti leaves unnamed.

Tirumular's chakra is drawn with eight lines across eight, a letter of the Lord set in the middle and the five letters recited quickly; Pambatti's Siddhars score the eight directions as chakras, set letters at the angles and recite the mantra. The procedure is the same in outline; Pambatti's chakra is peopled by the eight nagas instead of the fifty-one letters.

Pattinathar measures how far each possession follows the dead: property to the house, wife to the street, children to the burning ground; Pambatti asks whether country, house and cattle will seek one out when Yama comes, and answers that the cage once gone they are no use. Both end at the Lord's feet.

The Naladiyar's kings who rode elephants under moon-like umbrellas were carried off and spoken of as dead; Pambatti's elephants, armies, chariots and horses are no help when Yama comes. Both take the king's army as the strongest case of a protection that fails.

Pattinathar says the wealth kept hidden will not come when Yama breaks the frame and takes the life; Pambatti asks whether those who keep mountains of gold will sweep it up when Death comes. Pambatti adds the counter-claim that those whose heart rests on the Father do not perish.

Pattinathar: wife, children and wealth reach only one's own mouth, kin only as far as the cremation ground, and nothing is a companion for the road; Pambatti: children, wife, kin and sons-in-law do not die with one. Pattinathar asks what the companion is; Pambatti answers with the Maker who gave the world.

The Naladiyar's kin arrive unasked and leave wordlessly, leaving the body to its own people like a bird leaving its tree; Pambatti's kin simply do not die with the dying. Both state the limit of kinship as a fact of nature, without reproach.

The Naladiyar tells the lover not to desire the woman for her spear-like eyes, since she too will stoop over a staff; Pambatti says her beauty is turmeric fading in sunlight and the lover will flee when the body goes like the parrot from the silk-cotton pod. Both argue from the beauty's end to the desire's emptiness.

source_issues: 2014 names பதுமன் twice (மகத்தான பதுமன் and செய்ய பதுமன்); the eight nagas need மகாபதுமன் for one of them, so one name is probably corrupt or abbreviated.
2017 lines 1 and 2 are near-identical (அட்டதிக்குஞ் சக்கரங்க ளமைத்து விட்டோம் / அவ்வவற்றிற் சக்கரங்க ளமைத்து விட்டோம்), possibly a copyist's doubling.
2014 to 2018 drop the ஆடு பாம்பே refrain for சித்தனாரே; the section is in a different voice (address to Siddhars) and may be a separate piece interpolated into the kummi.
2021 line 3 ஆணிப் பொன்முத் தாரமம் பொன் அந்தகடகம் is overlong and garbled; read as ஆணிப்பொன் முத்தாரம் அம்பொன் அந்தக் கடகம்.

new_concepts.gloss: the void: the nothing that cannot be pointed at or shown, which the Siddhars name as the Real and claim to have caught; also, in the Siddhars' boasts, the sorcery or illusion they can show to followers
new_concepts.label_source: verses use the word (1987 பாழ் சூனியந்தன்னை, 2008 சூனியஞ் சொல்லிக் காட்டுவோம்)
